scope: Prepare Changes confirm proposals on main; do not apply foundation changes or manufacture authorization decisions.
date_basis: The four requested dates are author-directed story facts. January 15 is not presented as an independently verified historical release date.

sources.finding: Contemporary SSG notice explicitly identifies General Ledger as written in CBASIC for 8080/Z80 CP/M systems, with custom charts, departments, interactive validation and configurable reports. No numbered General Ledger release or runtime subversion is established.

sources.publication: Herbert R. Johnson archive: IMSAI C BASIC User’s Guide, 8 February 1978
sources.finding: Transcribes compiler CBASIC.COM 1.01 and runtime interpreter CRUN.COM 1.03. Establishes a period-correct intermediate-code execution environment and 14-digit arithmetic, not the exact versions supplied with SSG General Ledger.

SSG advertises 8080/Z80, 48K, dual disks, CP/M, keyboard, CRT and printer for its business software. Do not treat these later published requirements as a measured resource profile for the fictional June C port.
SSG advertisement identifies Keith Parsons as president and Alan Cooper as VP Systems Development. Their assigned July/August 1977 agreement and port-team roles are scenario choices.

review_decisions: SSG receives funded porting and tools assistance without equity, accounting-product ownership transfer, revenue share or buyback. No funding amount is invented.
The Academy is not a signatory in July 1977 because it is established later. Logix arranges the future channel and SSG-authorised training.
General Ledger replaces the five-module application scope. No SSG payroll, inventory, AR or AP implementation is claimed by these proposals.
The C port preserves ledger semantics and explicit decimal accuracy. Financial equivalence precedes same-configuration performance comparisons; there is no predicted speed ratio.

AION’s 1977 working compiler/interface baseline supports both internal applications and this port; later optimization/testing does not postpone all application development until the 1978 public IDE release.

The full morning event includes developer tools, the independently licensed General Ledger port, comparison and questions. Retire the separate afternoon event and move all live launch references atomically.

General Ledger’s proposed Aurelia distribution uses the existing one-diskette default for a single application; the old three-diskette default belonged to the replaced five-module suite. Image fit, working storage and single-drive swaps still require qualification.
Retain the later ERA/AIONix edition’s recorded 1981 first use; NCC 1980 shows the CP/M compatibility route rather than silently advancing native release.
Preserve Abacus’s independent fictitious payslip/layout demonstration but remove the implication that SSG General Ledger computes payroll. Its own demo exports ledger balances.

Preserve the later transactional server design and recovery limits, narrowing business operations to ledger journals/reversals. Each engineering phase ends with accepted delivery, maintainers trained, source/build handover and finite defect correction.

Stable legacy bpi record IDs and frozen legacy-schema keys remain internal identifiers only. Display names and current proposed story content identify SSG. No actor_relationship records are introduced.

The existing ecosystem-subject discussion is retargeted to the joint event, with its original snapshot preserved in discussion-before.json. No feedback history or annotation is resolved by preparing these proposals.

Existing authority and historical before/after snapshots remain immutable. The source product version is unspecified; 1.0 on the fictional AION C editions is a scenario label, not an asserted historical SSG version.
